evidence.summary: Taking a photo of a receipt fills in merchant, date and total; the user can correct any field.
Receipts in a foreign currency are converted to the user's home currency.
Scanned-receipt screen shows Merchant, Total in the receipt currency with an approximate home-currency amount (12.40 GBP, about 14.43 EUR) and Edit and Save actions; no date or category is shown.
The user reports (own use, on a phone) that after scanning the total is usually right but the date is often wrong and they fix it by hand.
People are invited to a budget by email; everyone in a budget sees its expenses; the budget owner can remove members.
Budget screen shows a named budget with member count, amount spent of a limit in one currency (412.30 of 600.00 EUR), the member list with the owner marked, and Invite and Remove member actions.
The user reports that after removing a member (Bo) from a budget, that member's earlier expenses stayed in the budget.
GET /v2/expenses filtered by budget_id returns expenses with id, merchant, amount, currency, date and category (no field types given).
POST /v2/expenses creates an expense; the request body is not documented.
GET /v2/budgets returns the budgets the token's user belongs to.
The API authenticates with a personal access token in the Authorization header and is limited to 60 requests per minute.

features.name: Receipt scanning
features.description: Photograph a receipt and have merchant, date and total filled in, then correct any field and save it as an expense.
features.observed_behaviour: Docs: photo -> merchant, date, total filled in; any field editable. Screenshot: result screen with merchant and total plus Edit and Save. User's notes: total usually right, date often wrong.
features.business_logic: Extracted fields: merchant, date, total. All fields user-editable before saving. Category is not documented as extracted.
features.integration: Needs an OCR or receipt-parsing engine (Tallyho's own is not documented), image upload and storage, and the expense store.

features.name: Foreign-currency conversion
features.description: Receipts in a foreign currency are converted to the user's home currency.
features.observed_behaviour: Scan screen shows the receipt total in its own currency and an approximate home-currency amount (12.40 GBP, about 14.43 EUR).
features.business_logic: Converts to the user's home currency. Rate source, rate date (receipt date or scan date) and rounding are unknown. Documented only for receipts.

features.name: Shared budgets
features.description: A budget several people belong to; every member sees all of its expenses and the amount spent against its limit.
features.observed_behaviour: Budget screen shows name, member count, spent of limit in one currency, member list with owner. API lists budgets the user belongs to and expenses per budget.
features.business_logic: Members see all expenses of the budget. One owner per budget (inferred from the single owner marker). A budget has a limit and a currency.
features.integration: Needs user accounts and a membership-based permission check on every budget and expense read.

features.name: Invite members by email
features.description: The budget's people invite others to it by email address.
features.observed_behaviour: Docs state email invitations; an Invite button is on the budget screen. The invitation email, acceptance flow and who may invite were not seen.
features.business_logic: Invite by email. Whether only the owner or any member can invite is unknown; expiry unknown.
features.integration: Needs outbound email and accounts for invitees.

features.name: Owner removes members
features.description: The budget owner can remove a member from the budget.
features.observed_behaviour: Remove member button on the budget screen; docs say the owner can remove members; the user saw a removed member's earlier expenses stay in the budget.
features.business_logic: Only the owner removes members. Removing a member keeps that member's existing expenses in the budget. Whether the removed member can still see them is unknown.
features.integration: Needs the permission model to drop the removed member's access.

features.name: Monthly budget reset
features.description: A budget's spending period restarts every month.
features.observed_behaviour: Documented in one line only; not seen happening.
features.business_logic: Monthly period. Whether expenses are kept (only the spent total restarts), the reset day, time zone, and rollover of unspent amounts are unknown.
features.integration: Spent total computed per calendar month, or a scheduled job.

features.name: Expense records
features.description: Create expenses and list a budget's expenses, each with merchant, amount, currency, date and category.
features.observed_behaviour: API: POST creates an expense; GET lists expenses by budget with id, merchant, amount, currency, date, category.
features.business_logic: Each expense belongs to a budget (filtered by budget_id). Field types, required fields and validation are not documented.
features.integration: The core record every other Tallyho feature writes or reads.

features.name: Public API with personal access tokens
features.description: A versioned HTTP API for expenses and budgets, authenticated with personal access tokens and rate-limited.
features.observed_behaviour: Documented only: three endpoints, token in the Authorization header, 60 requests per minute.
features.business_logic: Rate limit 60 requests per minute per token (scope of the limit inferred). Version prefix /v2.
features.integration: Needs token issuance and revocation, which are not documented.

features.name: Expense category field
features.observed_behaviour: Only the field name in the API response is documented; the set of categories, whether users can add their own, and whether scanning sets it are unknown.
features.integration: Category vocabulary must be chosen in the unified app.

auth.session: unknown for the app; Authorization header token for the API
auth.model: budget membership: every member sees the budget's expenses; the owner can remove members

unknowns: Which OCR or receipt-parsing engine Tallyho uses, and its accuracy; would be settled only by Tallyho's own disclosure (not needed: the unified app picks its own engine).
Whether scanning sets the category; the docs list only merchant, date and total. A test scan with the user present would settle it.
Tallyho's category list and whether users can add categories; the API names the field only. The user's own account would show it.

Exchange-rate provider, which date's rate is used (receipt date or scan date), rounding, and whether the original amount is kept; the scan screen shows both amounts. Help pages beyond the two supplied, or the user's account, would settle it.
What 'budgets reset monthly' means exactly: which day, which time zone, whether expenses are kept or only the spent total restarts, whether unspent amounts roll over.
Who may invite (owner only or any member), invitation expiry, and what an invitee without an account sees.
Whether a removed member can still see the expenses they added; whether the user regards expenses staying behind as desired or as a problem (their note does not say).
Whether a budget can have more than one owner, and whether ownership can be transferred.
App sign-in method, session mechanism and account model; only API personal access tokens are documented.
API field types, required fields, POST request body, pagination, error format, and how tokens are issued and revoked.
Where receipt images are stored and for how long.
Camera, capture and invite-acceptance screens; only two result screens were supplied.
